projects.title: Compact skills for language-model agents
projects.summary: Reproduced SoftSkill on Qwen3-8B, evaluating how 32 learned vectors compare with a long text skill across accuracy, context use, and evaluation reliability.
projects.problem: Long natural-language skill documents consume context. Can a compact learned representation retain their usefulness on a different language model?
contributions: Adapted the upstream SoftSkill research code to Qwen3-8B and compared learned skills, text instructions, and untrained initializations.
Reproduced the SearchQA comparison across three seeds and investigated the contribution of training versus initialization.
Identified a decoding-budget confound in LiveMath and documented the limits of a 200-question ToolQA pilot.
projects.evidence: The public repository reports 74.2 ± 0.3% SearchQA test-hard accuracy with 32 trained vectors, compared with 71.7% for a 1,995-token text skill and 67.9% without skills. This result is specific to that benchmark and evaluation setup.
projects.note: Reproduction and extension of Tao et al.’s SoftSkill method. The upstream method and code are credited in the repository; this is distinct from the EdgeAlign prototype.

projects.title: Learning skills from execution feedback
projects.summary: Designed forward-only reinforcement learning with evolution strategies over a 512-dimensional skill subspace.
projects.problem: Agents need ways to improve after deployment under constraints on compute and context. Updating compact skill representations is one way to study improvement without changing the full model.
contributions: Designed gradient-free optimization of learned agent skills using evolution strategies in a 512-dimensional subspace.
Developed prompt-embedding and execution support around Qwen3-8B and vLLM.
Investigated user feedback and tool-call outcomes as signals for skill improvement.
Worked on sandboxed evaluation, truncation diagnostics, and training stability.
projects.evidence: Prototype work on learned skill optimization, runtime support, and execution-based evaluation.
projects.note: Forward-only optimization and SoftSkill reproduction are separate research efforts.

projects.title: Rethinking one-token-at-a-time generation
projects.summary: Adapting pretrained Qwen models for masked diffusion and parallel multi-token generation, while reusing existing model weights.
projects.problem: Autoregressive generation proceeds one token at a time. Adapting a pretrained model to a masked-diffusion formulation offers a way to investigate parallel generation without starting training from scratch.
contributions: Adapting and fine-tuning Qwen-family models into an Auto-Regressive Masked Diffusion formulation.
Investigating parallel multi-token generation while preserving the value of pretrained weights.
Building on Karami and Ghodsi’s ARMD framework; the public QWEN-ARMDE repository provides related training and inference infrastructure.
projects.evidence: Ongoing research on masked-diffusion adaptation. The public QWEN-ARMDE repository contains related training and inference infrastructure.
projects.note: Building on Karami and Ghodsi’s Auto-Regressive Masked Diffusion framework.

projects.title: A memory that carries skills forward
projects.summary: Investigating gated low-rank updates to recurrent state so a frozen language model can carry useful task knowledge through tool use.
projects.problem: Repeated instructions are costly, and an agent’s task context can be lost as it interacts with tools. Recurrent state offers a different place to study reusable skills.
contributions: Implemented state capture, injection, and cache-aware serving for Qwen3.5-9B.
Verified recovery of the top-choice continuation in a controlled fp32 test.
Developing gated low-rank skill updates to frozen recurrent state.
Designing transfer studies on unseen tasks and skill combinations, comparing success, retention, and cost.
projects.evidence: State-handling implementation and a controlled continuation-recovery check are complete. Skill-update methods and broader transfer studies remain ongoing.
projects.note: Waterloo research on reusable memory through tool interactions.

projects.title: Giving documents a useful interface
projects.summary: Built a document-retrieval project around PDF ingestion, a local vector store, and an API for retrieval-grounded applications.
projects.problem: A collection of documents is useful only if relevant information can be retrieved and brought into a model’s context when needed.
contributions: Organized document ingestion and retrieval components in a Python application.
Used a local Chroma database to support experiments with document-based retrieval.
Built an API-oriented project structure for exploring retrieval-grounded applications.
projects.evidence: The public repository contains the implementation and a small set of research PDFs used for experimentation.
projects.note: Exploratory application with a local vector store and API.

projects.title: Longer context, practical computation
projects.summary: Developed and evaluated linear-attention variants, with reproducible latency/throughput measurements and GPU-aware implementations.
projects.problem: An architecture is useful only if its computational advantages survive implementation. Long-context research requires attention to both model behavior and GPU execution.
contributions: Implemented attention and Transformer architectures in a research training and evaluation stack.
Benchmarked latency and throughput under reproducible settings.
Adapted model blocks to existing Triton kernels and GPU-friendly dataflows.
projects.evidence: Academic research and implementation work. My FLA repository is a research fork of the upstream Flash Linear Attention project.
projects.note: Implementation builds on the upstream Flash Linear Attention project and its GPU kernels, linked below.

projects.title: Seeing beyond RGB
projects.summary: Built RGB–hyperspectral perception systems and sensor-fusion workflows that reduced manual-review costs by $200K annually.
projects.problem: Visual appearance alone is not enough to distinguish mineral structures reliably. Industrial workflows also need scalable processing and models that remain useful in production.
contributions: Developed and deployed models combining RGB imagery with hyperspectral measurements.
Worked on U-Net sulfide segmentation, pixel-accurate multimodal registration, and unsupervised mineral discovery.
Developed learnable spectral representations using RBF-style basis functions, alongside scalable training and distributed evaluation.
Led production troubleshooting for more than six months, coordinating failure analysis, fixes, and model-performance improvements.
projects.evidence: Across the multimodal perception work at EnerSoft, improved sensor fusion reduced annual manual-review costs by $200K. The work also included legacy-code refactoring and more reliable training and inference workflows.
projects.note: Industry work at EnerSoft, May 2022–December 2024. Company systems and datasets are not presented as public repositories.

projects.title: From road imagery to actionable inspection
projects.summary: Owned road-scene segmentation and anomaly detection from data curation to deployment, with human feedback driving model improvement.
projects.problem: Road imagery varies across conditions, and rare failures are precisely the cases an inspection workflow needs to surface. The data and retraining loop matter as much as the model.
contributions: Owned the modeling workflow from dataset curation and labeling strategy through training, evaluation, and deployment.
Developed a cascaded ResUNet–SAM3D approach for road-scene analysis.
Built human-in-the-loop annotation and active-learning workflows.
Analyzed recurring failures, prioritized edge cases, and incorporated corrected annotations into retraining.
projects.evidence: Industry work at Strayos, January–July 2026, spanning model development and the data feedback loop.
projects.note: Computer vision engineering at Strayos, January–July 2026.

projects.title: Inferring the dynamics behind neural signals
projects.summary: Developed a computational modeling and inference framework for short-term synaptic plasticity during deep brain stimulation.
projects.problem: Recorded neural responses contain information about how synapses change under stimulation. Recovering those dynamics requires a model that connects observations to the underlying processes.
contributions: Developed a computational framework and inference algorithm for short-term synaptic plasticity from neural recordings.
Connected stochastic modeling and signal processing to a biomedical research question during my master’s at the University of Toronto.
Worked with supervisors Milad Lankarany and Milos R. Popovic; the resulting research was published in PLOS ONE in 2022.
projects.evidence: Published paper: “Inferring stimulation induced short-term synaptic plasticity dynamics using novel dual optimization algorithm.”
projects.note: Master’s research at the University of Toronto; published in PLOS ONE in 2022.

projects.title: Learning identity from EEG
projects.summary: Designed a contrastive learning objective for identity-discriminative EEG representations and genuine-user versus impostor separation.
projects.problem: Useful EEG representations must capture distinguishing signals while accounting for the variability of neural measurements.
contributions: Designed a contrastive loss for EEG-based authentication.
Developed representation-learning methods that emphasize separation between individuals.
Investigated features intended to distinguish genuine-user and impostor representations.
projects.evidence: Method-development experience in EEG authentication. Separate collaborative work on EEG foundation-model soft biometrics is listed among manuscripts in preparation.
projects.note: Research on contrastive representations for EEG authentication.

projects.title: From physiological signals to working prototypes
projects.summary: Combined adaptive filtering, Kalman methods, and wearable sensing across maternal–fetal ECG separation and an ECG–PPG prototype.
projects.problem: Physiological measurements mix sources and noise. Useful monitoring begins with both a reliable acquisition path and signal-processing methods that recover the information of interest.
contributions: Applied adaptive and Kalman filtering to separate maternal and fetal ECG signals.
Designed a single-arm ECG and PPG measurement circuit for my undergraduate final project.
Integrated signal acquisition with Android communication.
projects.evidence: Academic project work spanning signal separation and a wearable sensing prototype at Amirkabir University of Technology.
projects.note: Academic research and a sensing prototype; the wearable system was my undergraduate final project.

projects.title: Learning to add color
projects.summary: Implemented a conditional GAN in PyTorch for image colorization, connecting representation learning with image-to-image generation.
projects.problem: Colorization asks a model to generate plausible chromatic information while remaining consistent with the structure of an input image.
contributions: Implemented a conditional GAN for image colorization in PyTorch.
Explored conditional generation as a deep-learning final project.
projects.evidence: Implemented as part of a deep-learning final project.

projects.title: Exploring generative data for perception
projects.summary: Explored conditional generative models for augmenting hyperspectral geological imagery used in perception workflows.
projects.problem: Specialized industrial imagery can be scarce. Conditional generation offers a way to explore additional training examples while respecting the structure of the source data.
contributions: Worked on a conditional GAN approach to generate hyperspectral geological imagery.
Explored its use as data augmentation for downstream perception models.
projects.evidence: Explored generated hyperspectral examples as additional data for perception workflows.

projects.title: Representations across pose and appearance
projects.summary: Combined RGB inputs and landmark heatmaps in face-recognition experiments, with pose, image quality, and baseline comparisons.
projects.problem: Pose and image quality create difficult failure modes for recognition. Landmark information provides an additional representation to test against RGB-only baselines.
contributions: Built a modular PyTorch project combining RGB images and landmark heatmap channels.
Supported ArcFace/CosFace heads, optional masks, and aligned transforms.
Explored landmark autoencoding and evaluated recognition across varying pose and image quality.
projects.evidence: Public code includes ablations, classification/verification metrics, and experiment notebooks.
projects.note: Open-source experiments with recognition baselines and ablations.

projects.title: Making a model reproducible to run
projects.summary: Packaged a vision model as a containerized FastAPI service with automated checks and reproducible deployment workflows.
projects.problem: A trained model is only one part of a usable system. Packaging, interfaces, and repeatable checks make the implementation easier to run and change.
contributions: Built a containerized FastAPI service for MNIST inference.
Structured the Python package for reproducible installation and execution.
Added GitHub Actions checks around the implementation.
projects.evidence: Public repository with the service implementation and CI configuration.
projects.note: An engineering demonstration built around a small vision model.
